parsed.headline: President Mahama arrives in Moscow for third Russia–Africa Summit

pages.text: President John Dramani Mahama of Ghana arrived in Moscow on Monday to lead a delegation to the third Russia–Africa Summit. The summit, hosted by Russian President Vladimir Putin, is scheduled for October 28–29, 2026, and is expected to include more than 30 African heads of state and government. According to presidential aide Yuri Ushakov, 48 African countries have confirmed their participation. The summit is expected to focus on peace diplomacy, security cooperation, and equitable economic partnerships. President Mahama is also scheduled to participate in an Economic and Humanitarian Forum and is expected to hold high-level bilateral talks with President Putin on the margins of the summit, a prospect confirmed by Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa. Additionally, President Mahama is expected to grant an audience to various Russian businesses and state institutions, and two Russian universities—the Russian University of Transport and the Peoples’ Friendship University of Russia—are scheduled to separately confer honorary doctorate degrees on him during ceremonies in Moscow. Ghana's Ambassador to Russia, Dr Koma Steem Jehu-Appiah, led embassy staff to receive the President at the airport, where Russian government officials were also present.

Speaking at the Financial Times Africa Summit on October 21, President Mahama stated he would use the Moscow visit to attempt to convince President Putin to agree to a ceasefire in the four-year-old Russia–Ukraine war. He framed this appeal within Ghana's non-aligned foreign policy, describing the nation as being among the 'friends to all and enemies to none.' The President noted that Accra maintains cordial relations with the United States, the European Union, China, and Russia, arguing that this balanced posture allows for engagement with Moscow on peace matters without taking sides. Separately, Moscow is hosting the eighth summit of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum on October 27 to discuss global energy market developments. The Russia–Africa Summit is expected to be co-chaired by President Putin and Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye, the current chair of the African Union.

parsed.headline: Israelis to vote in first national election since October 7 attack

pages.text: Israelis are scheduled to vote on October 20, 2026, in the country’s first national election since the Hamas attack on October 7, 2023. According to reporting by Africanews, the campaign is characterized by deep divisions, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s leadership, national security, and the country's future serving as central issues. The election is widely viewed as a referendum on Netanyahu’s management of security failures related to the October 7 attack and subsequent wars, as well as his government's domestic policies. Campaign topics include the cost of living, military service exemptions for ultra-Orthodox Jews, and a judicial overhaul that critics claim weakened Israel's democratic institutions. While divisions exist regarding Netanyahu's leadership, the report notes that Israel's military operations in Gaza and across the region have received relatively little debate during the campaign. Both major political blocs broadly support Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank and oppose the establishment of a Palestinian state. For many voters, the election represents an opportunity to address societal divisions and determine the nation's direction. Gadi Eisenkot, a 66-year-old former military chief of staff and centrist challenger to Netanyahu, has pledged to investigate the failures of the October 7 attack and work to restore Israel's standing with international allies. Eisenkot, who rose through the military ranks over four decades, lost his son and two nephews in combat in Gaza following the October 7 attacks.

parsed.headline: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva wins Brazil presidential runoff election

pages.text: Incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has secured a fourth term in Brazil following a second-round presidential runoff election. According to the Superior Electoral Court, Lula received 51.79% of the valid votes, defeating challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, who received 48.21%. This result marks the first time in Brazilian electoral history that a first-round verdict has been overturned, as Bolsonaro had led in the first round of voting earlier this month. The victory makes Lula the country's longest-serving leader. Following the announcement, thousands of supporters celebrated in cities such as São Paulo, where crowds gathered on Paulista Avenue on October 25, 2026. Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has refused to accept the result and stated he would seek to have it annulled. The former president, Jair Bolsonaro, is currently serving a 27-year jail term for his role in an attempted coup following the previous presidential election. During the election process, a Supreme Court judge extended polling time by two hours after both candidates requested the extension. Additionally, Lula's campaign accused opponents of sabotaging public transport to prevent voters from reaching the polls.

The election result triggered significant volatility in Brazilian financial markets. Following the announcement, the Brazilian real dropped 12 percent against the United States dollar in spot trading. On Monday, Bovespa stock index futures tumbled nearly 15 percent, and the Bovespa index fell 10 percent from its previous close, triggering a 30-minute trading halt via a circuit-breaker mechanism. Rachel Ziemba, an adjunct senior fellow at the Center for a New American Security, told Al Jazeera that traders are covering bets that assumed a Bolsonaro victory and tighter fiscal policy, noting that market pressure is amplified by Bolsonaro's refusal to concede. This follows a period of market growth; on October 23, 2026, stocks closed almost 7 percent above their levels prior to the first round, while the real was nearly 5 percent stronger against the dollar.

parsed.headline: Bangladesh and Japan seek expanded trade and investment ties during official visit

pages.text: During a four-day official visit to Tokyo that began on October 26, 2026, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Japanese officials discussed strengthening bilateral trade and investment. The visit, made at the invitation of Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, included a meeting between Tarique and Masumi Kakinoki, chairman of Marubeni Corporation and president of the Japan-Bangladesh Committee for Commercial and Economic Cooperation. Kakinoki stated that the effective implementation of the Economic Partnership Agreement could expand bilateral trade, increase Japanese investment, and create new business opportunities, according to BSS reports. Upon his arrival, Tarique was received by Japanese State Minister for Foreign Affairs Yasutaka Nakasone. Tarique is scheduled to hold a bilateral summit with Takaichi on October 27, 2026.

Tarique sought Japanese investment to modernize the Karnaphuli Fertiliser Company Limited and to explore establishing a second fertilizer factory in Bangladesh. He also requested investment in advanced manufacturing, renewable energy, and information and communication technology, noting that the government is working to reform regulations and simplify approval procedures to create an investment-friendly environment. Officials expect the two countries to sign between five and eight agreements covering sectors such as agriculture, civil aviation, infrastructure, energy cooperation, and official security assistance for the Bangladesh Coast Guard. These agreements are expected to include memorandums of understanding regarding upazila-level development and business climate improvements.

According to officials, the two nations are expected to agree on approximately $2 billion in loans and financial support, which includes $300 million in budgetary support. While Bangladesh is expected to seek development cooperation and investment, Japan is likely to focus on energy, maritime security, and regional connectivity. Additionally, the Japanese power generation company JERA is expected to assist in developing energy reserve infrastructure under the Moheshkhali Integrated Development Initiative.

pages.text: A JoyNews Research investigation has identified what appear to be forged signatures and discrepancies in payment records related to a government-funded evacuation of hundreds of Ghanaians from South Africa. parsed.headline: Syrian Airlines to resume direct flights between Berlin and Damascus in November

pages.text: Syrian Airlines announced on October 26, 2026, that direct flights between Berlin and Damascus will resume next month. The first nonstop flight is scheduled to take off on Nov. 10, marking the airline’s first service connecting Germany with the Syrian Arab Republic in more than a decade. The airline had previously halted flights to Europe during the Syrian civil war, which began in 2011 and ended in December 2024 following the fall of President Bashar Assad and his regime during an opposition advance. According to the Syrian Arab News Agency, Syria’s General Authority for Civil Aviation and Air Transport stated the decision would make it easier for the approximately 1 million Syrians living in Germany to visit or return to their home country.

The resumption of service follows recent activity by German carriers. In July, Leav Aviation began flying from Dusseldorf to Damascus, and in August, Sundair launched its first direct flight between Berlin and Damascus. During the civil war, major international airlines canceled flights to Syria, and travelers were often forced to travel overland to airports in Lebanon and Jordan to fly abroad.

pages.text: BNP Paribas Asset Management has been increasing its positions in long-dated Japanese government bonds (JGBs), citing a steep yield curve and indications of returning domestic demand in the market. McAlevey noted that the sector has recently “significantly outperformed other global long ends,” offering a source of diversification.

parsed.headline: Student-led movement wins parliamentary elections in Serbia as Aleksandar Vučić concedes

pages.text: In Serbia's parliamentary elections, the Student List, a youth-led movement that emerged from protests, claimed victory, pushing longtime leader Aleksandar Vučić and his Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) into second place. Following Vučić's concession, celebrations occurred in Belgrade, Novi Sad, and other cities. According to the election commission, with 97% of polling stations counted, the Student List secured 2.25 million votes (52.7%), while the SNS received 1.67 million votes (39.2%). Projections indicated the Student List would take between 135 and 140 seats, compared to approximately 105 for the SNS. Most opposition parties stood aside to allow the Student List a clear run in the election. The student movement formed less than two years ago following a railway station canopy collapse in Novi Sad that killed 16 people, an event blamed on corruption and negligence. Ilija Srdanović, the physician leading the Student List's 250 candidates, stated the movement hopes to free the country from tyranny and move toward a more civilized Serbia. In his concession speech, Vučić stated, “It is clear we have lost these elections.” He attributed the loss to independent media and alleged interference from unnamed European countries and the “US deep state.” Vučić, who had served two terms as president and could not seek a third, had led the SNS with the aim of returning to the post of prime minister. The election results mark an end to more than a decade of rule by Vučić and the SNS.

parsed.headline: Ga Mantse to chair 30th GJA Awards in Ghana

pages.text: King Tackie Teiko Tsuru II, the Ga Mantse, is scheduled to chair the 30th anniversary edition of the Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards. On October 23, 2026, GJA President Albert Kwabena Dwumfour led a national executive delegation to the Ga Mantse's palace in Kaneshie, Accra, to formally extend the invitation. The ceremony is scheduled to take place at the Accra International Conference Centre’s Grand Arena. While the Ga Mantse will chair the event, the Asantehene, Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, serves as the patron for the awards, marking the first time two prominent traditional rulers will share the spotlight at a single GJA event. The GJA selected the Ga Mantse for the role, citing his previous mediation of a 2021 election dispute that stalled the association's national polls for nearly a year. The 30th edition marks three decades since the GJA instituted the awards to recognize excellence in journalism.
